predecessors.name: French Algeria
predecessors.text: Algeria: the three civil territories of Alger, Oran and Constantine, 'organized as Departments of France' by the 1848 Constitution (French Algeria page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Libya
successors.text: the Fezzan-Ghadames military territory, which joined Tripolitania and Cyrenaica 'to form the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December 1951'

successors.name: Morocco
successors.text: the French zone of the protectorate, ended by the Franco-Moroccan declaration of 2 March 1956

successors.name: French Fifth Republic
successors.text: all the remaining colonial territories in Africa (Algeria, French West Africa, French Equatorial Africa, Madagascar, Cameroon, Togo, Somaliland, the Comoros), which Cliopatria carries on in the Fifth…

ledger.x: 1846: French Africa begins as the Senegal river posts, the Gabon estuary and Mayotte.
1848: Algeria becomes part of France.
1849: the Gabon estuary grows by 13 cells (about 3,300 km2).
1853: 11 more Senegal cells (about 2,800 km2).
1856: 6 cells on the upper Senegal river (Mali).
1859: the Senegal river basin grows by about 25,000 km2.
1860: the north bank of the Senegal is added.
1863: the Kingdom of Porto-Novo accepts French protection.
1865: the first Porto-Novo protectorate ends.
1868: Cotonou becomes a French protectorate.
1870: the Algerian cells rise from 9% to 20% of modern Algeria.
1880: the French establish the Upper River colony on the upper Senegal.
24 April 1881: French troops enter Tunisia from the north.
12 May 1881: the Treaty of Bardo ends the Bey's resistance as a state.
12 May 1881: Tunisia becomes a French protectorate.
1882: Porto-Novo becomes a French protectorate again.
1884: France occupies Guinea.
1885: 340 more Senegal and Mali cells and a few on the Ivory Coast and the Benin coast.
March 1885: France takes protectorates over the Somali clans of the Gulf of Tadjoura.
17 December 1885: Antsiranana (Diego-Suarez) is ceded to France.
1890: the Ivory Coast coast and a first strip of the Central African Republic are added.
4 March 1890: Dahomey storms the French stockade at Cotonou.
3 October 1890: the first war ends in a treaty.
3 October 1890: Dahomey cedes Cotonou to France.
4 July 1892: the second Franco-Dahomean war begins.
8 December 1892: the Franco-Liberian treaty fixes the frontier of French Ivory Coast on the Cavalla River.
1894: the Sultanate of Bangassou becomes a French protectorate.
15 January 1894: Béhanzin surrenders and the war ends.
15 January 1894: Dahomey falls and passes to France.
12 December 1894: the French take Tamatave and open the second war on Madagascar.
1895: the French Congo, Gabon and the Ubangi lands are drawn as French.
1895: the Algerian cells rise from 20% to 40% of modern Algeria.
1 October 1895: the French enter Antananarivo.
1 October 1895: Madagascar becomes a French protectorate.
27 October 1895: the federation of French West Africa is founded.
ledger.cp: Ivory Coast and Upper Niger chiefdoms

ledger.x: 1897: the French depose Queen Ranavalona III and dissolve the Merina monarchy; the protectorate becomes a colony.
1897: Madagascar is French land.
1897: Dar al Kuti becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Dar al Kuti (protectorate): 1897'); France annexed it in 1912.
1899: the Sultanate of Damagaram (Zinder) becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Sultanate of Damagaram (protectorate): 1899').
1900: Chad is organised.
1902: a French military expedition enters the Hoggar.
1902: the Emirate of Trarza becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Emirate of Trarza (protectorate): 1902'); the same list gives 'Senegambia and Niger: 1902-1904'.
1903: the conquest of the Algerian Sahara ends.
1903: the Algerian Sahara is French.
1905: the Sahara and Sahel interior is drawn as French West Africa.
1905: the Taganit confederation's emirate becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Taganit confederation's emirate (protectorate): 1905').
18 September 1907: a second Franco-Liberian treaty moves the northern frontier south to its present line.
29 May 1908: the first dated French victory over Wadai forces, at Dokotchi.
1909: the Emirate of Adrar becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Adrar emirate (protectorate): 1909'); Cliopatria already draws all of Mauritania from 1905.
June 1909: the French take Abéché.
October 1911: Dud Murra surrenders.
November 1911: France cedes a slice of the Middle Congo to Germany after the Agadir Crisis.
1912: Dar al Kuti ceases to be a protectorate.
1912: France annexes Dar al Kuti.
1912: the occupation becomes annexation.
1912: Wadai is annexed to French Chad.
30 March 1912: Morocco becomes a French protectorate.
6 August 1914: the Allies invade German Kamerun.
6 August 1914: French troops land in German Togoland.
27 August 1914: Togoland surrenders.
27 August 1914: Britain and France occupy Togoland.
1915: French and Belgian troops occupy Neukamerun.
February 1916: France and Britain agree to divide Kamerun.
10 March 1916: the Kamerun campaign ends in Allied victory.
1919: the occupation of Neukamerun ends with the peace settlement.
1919: Neukamerun is French land again, inside the AEF colonies.
1919: the French zone becomes the League of Nations mandate of French Cameroon (Paris Peace Conference).
1919: French Cameroon becomes French land under the League of Nations mandate.
20 July 1922: French Togoland becomes a League of Nations mandate.
20 July 1922: French Togoland becomes French land under the League of Nations mandate.
August 1940: French Cameroon rallies to the Free French.
August 1940: Chad, Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari rally to the Free French.
November 1940: the Free French attack Vichy Gabon.
12 November 1940: Gabon falls to the Free French.
12 November 1940: Gabon passes to the Free French.
November 1942: Axis forces occupy the east of Tunisia.
28 December 1942: Britain occupies French Somaliland.
1943: French rule returns to Djibouti.
1943: the Free French lands rejoin the shape.
January 1943: Free French forces from Chad take the Fezzan.
13 May 1943: the last Axis forces in Tunisia surrender.
27 October 1946: the French Empire becomes the French Union.
24 December 1951: the Fezzan passes to the Kingdom of Libya.
2 March 1956: France recognises Moroccan independence.
20 March 1956: Tunisia becomes independent.
1957: Cliopatria's French Africa row ends and its land continues in the French Fifth Republic row from 1958.

wars.name: French conquest of Tunisia
wars.outcome: French victory: the Treaty of Bardo of 12 May 1881 makes Tunisia a protectorate; the Sfax revolt (June-July 1881) and Kairouan (August-October) are put down and 'May 1882: Occupation of the whole country was completed'.

wars.name: Franco-Hova Wars
wars.outcome: First war 1883-1885: the Treaty of Tamatave (17 December 1885) cedes Diego-Suarez and gives France Malagasy foreign policy.

wars.name: French conquest of the Sudan
wars.outcome: 'French conquest began in 1879'; the Upper River colony 'Established c.

wars.name: First Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: by the treaty of 3 October 1890 Dahomey cedes Cotonou and recognises Porto-Novo as a French protectorate.

wars.name: Second Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: French troops entered Abomey on 17 November 1892 and Béhanzin surrendered on 15 January 1894; Dahomey became French (the page lists 'French Dahomey' from 1894).

wars.name: Mokrani Revolt
wars.outcome: 'The most serious native insurrection since the time of Abd al-Qadir was the 1871 Mokrani Revolt in the Kabylia'; 'By April 1871, 250 tribes had risen'; the surviving commanders were tried in Constantine in 1873.

wars.name: French conquest of the Algerian Sahara
wars.outcome: 'In 1902, a French military expedition entered Hoggar Mountains and defeated Kel Ahaggar in a battle in Tit'; 'The conquest of the Saharan lands in Algeria finished in 1903'.

wars.name: Wadai War
wars.outcome: French victory: Abéché occupied in June 1909, Dud Murra surrendered in October 1911 and 'Wadai was completely occupied by the French in 1912'.

wars.name: Agadir Crisis
wars.outcome: Diplomatic: 'the deployment of the German gunboat Panther to the port of Agadir in July 1911'; in November 1911 Germany accepted France's position in Morocco 'in return for a slice of territory in the French Equatorial African colony of Middle Congo'.

wars.name: Togoland campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: French troops landed at Little Popo on 6 August 1914, the colony was invaded on 26 August and surrendered 'without conditions' on 27 August 1914; divided into French and British zones on 27 December 1916.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory ('6 August 1914 - 10 March 1916'): Douala surrendered on 27 September 1914, the Germans withdrew to Spanish Río Muni in early 1916; Britain and France agreed to divide Kamerun in February 1916 and the League of Nations mandates followed in 1919.

wars.name: Rif War
wars.outcome: 'A coalition of France and Spain finally defeated the rebels in 1925'; Lyautey's tenure ran 'in the middle of the failed revolt of the Republic of the Rif'.

wars.name: Battles of Dakar
wars.outcome: French West Africa 'declared allegiance to the Vichy regime' against the Free French Forces 'in July and September 1940' (the two battles of Dakar).

wars.name: Battle of Gabon
wars.outcome: Free French victory: 'Gabon fell to Free France after the Battle of Gabon in November 1940'; 'Gabon instead remained loyal to Vichy France until 12 November 1940'.

wars.name: Tunisia campaign
wars.outcome: Axis forces held the east of Tunisia from November 1942 (campaign 17 November 1942 to 13 May 1943); Tunis and Bizerte fell on 7 May and the last Axis surrender was on 13 May 1943, when the Bey was also deposed by Free French authorities.

wars.name: Free French occupation of the Fezzan
wars.outcome: Free French forces from Chad 'moved north from Chad to take control of the territory in January 1943' with British approval; administered until 24 December 1951.

wars.name: Algerian War
wars.outcome: Clipped to this dossier's end (1957) by the reviewer; the war continues in the french-fifth-republic dossier.

certainty.note: Coastal posts, river basins and the Algerian south have no surveyed limits on the pages opened; the Tunisian protectorate of 1881 is the one fixed state, its frontiers not on the pages.

Colony boundaries follow decrees (Mauritania and Niger 1904, Upper Volta 1921), treaties (Fes 1912, the November 1911 cession of Neukamerun) and agreed partition lines (Kamerun February 1916, Togoland 27 December 1916).
